commits.message: fix(proc): a launch concludes with its group and leaves the holder its pipes (candybar-testing-0x6u.425)
fix(proc): a launch ends with its group, not with whoever holds its pipes (candybar-testing-0x6u.425)

test(diagnostics): a config folder the OS refuses shows on every bar drawn from its entry (brandon-unfiled-3248.fyvh)

candybar-plugins-vf6g.8uk (#507) carried a refused config directory to the
indicator, but only the link-chain half was proven at a drawn bar. This
drives a refusal through the daemon's own render to the ⚠, the viewer and
the render event, over a failed load too.

fix(daemon): a request's timers run on its clock, and the deadline case holds them (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3) (#533)

* fix(test): a render's event records the wait it armed, and the deadline case reads that (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)

The case asserted Date.now() <= deadline right after the reply, which
times the test worker's loop: on PR #474's CI it read 47 ms past. The
unstated branch made the same comparison against a tighter bound.

RequestWait carried one fact twice, `ms` for the event and `endsAt` for
the timer, so `deadline=` could disagree with the wait that ran. `ms` is
gone, and the event notes the value `waitWithin` is armed with.

The case now reads that figure and its bound, with no clock read after
the reply. Nothing left about it is the process's, so it moves back to
the worker. `/^stated:\d+ms$/` is gone with it: a request read late
records a negative budget, and that regex refused it.

test/wait-within.test.ts gains the case that times when a wait ends. The
existing ones said only which arm ended it.

* fix(daemon): a request's timers run on its clock, so a held daemon holds them (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)

A budget was figured from DaemonClock while the wait and the backstop ran on
real setTimeout, so a held clock could not own a request's time. `after` on the
clock gives both one owner: the deadline case holds its daemon and advances to
exact figures, a stall in the worker can no longer reach the backstop first, and
arming the wait with anything but its budget fails the case.

From the high review: RequestWait goes, since `stated` was req.deadline.kind, and
the process file's one case stops carrying shared fixtures.

* fix(daemon): a held clock fires as a real one does, and an answered request's backstop is cleared (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)

* test(daemon): the answered-request case holds its client open, so it can fail (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)

* fix(test): the claims about a held clock say what it holds, and the case drops what it cannot show (brandon-unfiled-3248.a5k3)
